title: Approximation theorems for fermionic Gaussian states
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Farzin Salek, Zoltán Zimborás, Aram Harrow, Patrick Hayden, Jens Eisert
abstract: A recurring principle in many-body physics is that sufficiently distributed interactions or correlations lead to an effectively mean-field description. For fermionic Gaussian states, we establish a quantitative version of this principle directly at the level of Majorana covariance matrices. The main observation is that the admissibility condition for fermionic covariance matrices imposes a quantitative monogamy constraint on two-point correlations: a fixed region has only a bounded covariance budget to distribute among many disjoint regions. We use this principle in three directions. First, for quadratic fermionic Hamiltonians on finite simple graphs of high degree, we obtain product-state approximations to both the ground-state energy and the finite-temperature free energy, with error of order \(D^{-1/2}\) for \(D\)-regular graphs. Second, we prove a finite fermionic Gaussian de Finetti theorem: a \(k\)-copy Gaussian state that is \(n\)-exchangeable under graded fermionic copy permutations is \(O(k/n)\)-close in trace norm to the product of its one-copy marginal. In particular, infinite exchangeability within the Gaussian class implies exact product structure. Third, for spatial fermionic Gaussian states with exponentially clustering mutual information, we prove that the conditional mutual information across a separating buffer decays as \(O(r^{-1})\), and hence, by recoverability, the state admits an \(O(r^{-1/2})\) trace-norm approximation by a recovered state. These results show that product and de Finetti approximations and recoverability estimates for fermionic Gaussian systems can all be derived directly from covariance-level structure.
summary: This work develops quantitative approximation theorems for fermionic Gaussian states by analyzing constraints on their covariance matrices. It shows that structural properties like high connectivity, exchangeability, or spatial separation force the state to be close to a product state. These results provide powerful, covariance-based tools for approximating complex many-body systems.
main_problem: To establish quantitative approximation theorems for fermionic Gaussian states, showing that structural constraints force the state to be close to a simpler, product-like state.
main_result: The paper derives product-state approximations for high-degree graphs, proves a finite fermionic Gaussian de Finetti theorem, and establishes $O(r^{-1/2})$ trace-norm recoverability estimates for spatially clustering states.
method: The analysis is conducted directly at the level of the Majorana covariance matrix, leveraging a core 'covariance monogamy' constraint.
model_or_system: The system is fermionic Gaussian states, which are characterized by their covariance matrix and arise from quadratic, noninteracting fermionic Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Covariance matrices, ground-state energy, finite-temperature free energy, conditional mutual information $I_ho(A : C | B)$.
important_parameters: Graph degree $D$, copy number $k$, separation distance $r$, and the error scaling $O(D^{-1/2})$ or $O(r^{-1/2})$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the Gaussian class of states, and the high-degree results apply to quadratic Hamiltonians.
paper_structure: The paper builds its results by showing that the covariance-level structure imposes a monogamy constraint, which is then applied in three distinct physical contexts: high connectivity (energy approximation), exchangeability (de Finetti theorem), and spatial separation (recoverability estimates).
why_interesting: The direct derivation of approximation bounds from covariance-level structure provides powerful, quantitative tools for understanding how local correlations dictate global thermodynamic properties in many-body systems.
